extra.message: User input from request.GET['packet_ref'] is concatenated with BASE_EXPORT_DIR to construct a file path, then read via parcel_path.read_text(). Path traversal sequences like '../../etc/passwd' allow reading arbitrary files on the filesystem.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User input from request.GET['expr'] is passed directly to eval(). Although __builtins__ is set to {}, Python object introspection (e.g.,().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()) can bypass this sandbox, enabling arbitrary code execution.

User-controlled data from request.body or request.GET['blob'] is deserialized using pickle.loads(), which can execute arbitrary code during deserialization. An attacker can craft a pickle payload to achieve remote code execution.

User input from request.GET['fragment'] is interpolated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered. This allows Server-Side Template Injection, enabling remote code execution through Jinja2's object traversal capabilities.

User input from request.GET['url'] is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen() without URL validation or allowlisting. An attacker can make the server issue HTTP requests to arbitrary internal or external URLs, enabling SSRF attacks to access internal services.

User-controlled JSON from request.body is parsed and used directly as a MongoDB query filter in find_one(query) without sanitization. An attacker can craft a query with MongoDB operators (e.g., {'$gt': ''}) to bypass filters or extract unauthorized data.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: XML parser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, and parses user-supplied request.body. This enables XML External Entity attacks, allowing an attacker to read arbitrary files or make network requests from the server.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User input from request.GET['name'] is concatenated with BASE_EXPORT_DIR to construct a file path, then request.body is written to that path via target.write_bytes(). Path traversal sequences like '../../tmp/shell.py' allow writing arbitrary files on the filesystem.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Authorization is based on a client-controlled cookie (ops_badge) or header (x-ops-badge) compared against the hardcoded value 'lead'. Any client can set these values to gain elevated access, bypassing proper server-side authentication.

The request Origin header is reflected back into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests, effectively bypassing the same-origin policy and enabling cross-site request forgery and data theft.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The Authorization header (containing Bearer tokens or API keys) is logged in plain text via logger.warning(). This exposes sensitive credentials in application logs, making them accessible to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: X-XSS-Protection is set to '0' and Content-Security-Policy is set to an empty string, explicitly disabling browser XSS protections and content security policy. This removes defense-in-depth protections against cross-site scripting attacks.

Environment variables including DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and the server's base export directory path are returned in the JSON response. This leaks internal server configuration details that could aid further attacks.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: ssl._create_unverified_context() creates an SSL context that disables certificate verification, and this context is used with urllib.request.urlopen(). This allows man-in-the-middle attacks on the outbound HTTPS connection.
Verification codes ('4812', '5930') are hardcoded in source code. Anyone with access to the source can bypass this authentication mechanism.

The Django SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded value 'dev-only-change-me-hr-payroll-portal-not-for-production' when the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. This known key can be used to forge session cookies and CSRF tokens.

DEBUG mode defaults to True via env_bool('DJANGO_DEBUG', True). If DJANGO_DEBUG is not explicitly set to 'false' in the environment, the application runs in DEBUG mode, exposing detailed error pages with sensitive information including stack traces, settings, and database queries.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The request_status view allows authorized users to set any valid HRRequestStatus value directly (line 739: hr_request.status = status) without validating that the transition is legal. An employee who passes the can_change_hr_request check (which allows access when status is OPEN or WAITING_ON_EMPLOYEE) can directly set status to RESOLVED or CLOSED, bypassing the intended workflow.
